md_name: Fungal biosynthetic gene cluster and metabolite discovery workflow
md_description: This DAG captures the experimental and computational workflow for studying fungal biosynthetic gene clusters and their secondary metabolites. It starts from fungal cultures or biomass, generates genomic and chemical measurements, processes sequencing and metabolomics data, annotates biosynthetic genes and clusters, and integrates both branches to discover novel secondary metabolites and understand their biosynthetic genetic architecture.

fungal_culture.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the starting fungal biological material and excluded any protocol, sequencing, extraction, capture, or computational details that belong downstream. Since this is the root biological object in the workflow, the schema focuses on identity/origin and the culture state needed to interpret both genomic DNA and metabolite outputs. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no duplication constraints to apply beyond staying within entity territory. I avoided sample/subject/experiment identifiers if they would likely be repeated elsewhere, and instead chose concise origin and cultivation descriptors that help downstream users understand what the fungal biomass was.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the fungal isolate or culture used as the starting material in this workflow; use a stable lab ID or accession-style string such as 'FUNG-001'. Record once for the biological source of both DNA and metabolite branches.

Taxonomic identification of the fungus at the finest resolved rank available from the source culture, reported as a string such as genus_species or a higher taxonomic label if unresolved; measured/assigned at the time the culture is registered.

Origin of the fungal culture used in the experiment, describing where the isolate came from before any downstream processing. Use a controlled categorical label to distinguish source context for interpretation of genomic and chemical diversity.

Primary source material from which the fungal isolate was obtained, such as fruiting body, soil, plant tissue, or pre-existing culture. Record as a concise free-text string at sample registration time.

Growth medium or substrate on which the fungal biomass was maintained prior to DNA extraction and metabolite isolation, for example PDA, malt extract agar, or liquid broth. Record the medium used for the culture that produced the analyzed biomass.

Incubation or growth temperature of the fungal culture used to generate the starting biomass, reported in degrees Celsius at the time the biomass was harvested. Typical values are organism-dependent and often fall between 15 and 37.

Length of time the fungal culture was grown before biomass harvest, reported in days. Record the actual cultivation period used to obtain material for DNA extraction and metabolite analysis; typical ranges are about 2 to 60 days depending on growth rate.

Physical state of the fungal material used as input to downstream workflows, indicating whether the starting object was actively growing mycelium, sporulated culture, fruiting tissue, or mixed biomass. Use this to interpret DNA yield and metabolite content.

Identifier for the biological replicate or independently grown culture unit corresponding to this starting fungal biomass; use a string such as 'replicate_1'. This supports linking one culture to multiple downstream assays.

dna_extraction.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only how the fungal biomass was transformed into genomic DNA: extraction method, key reagent/kit details, lysis conditions, yield, purity, and extraction outcome quality. I excluded entity-level source information from fungal_culture and excluded downstream DNA library or sequencing settings, since those belong to later nodes. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I did not need to suppress duplicates beyond avoiding overlap with the fungal_culture schema. I also avoided describing the DNA molecule itself beyond process output quality indicators, because the purified DNA entity is a separate node.

md_schema.descr: Primary extraction workflow used to isolate genomic DNA from the fungal material, recorded at the time of processing; examples include phenol-chloroform, silica column, magnetic bead, or CTAB-based protocols. Use this to reproduce the isolation procedure.

Commercial kit or named reagent system used for DNA isolation, if applicable, recorded during the extraction step; example format: 'Qiagen DNeasy Plant Mini Kit'. Leave empty or use 'none' if a kit was not used.

Key composition of the lysis buffer used during fungal cell disruption and DNA release, reported as a concise string with salient components and concentrations when known, such as 'CTAB, NaCl, EDTA, Tris-HCl, beta-mercaptoethanol'.

Temperature used during the extraction incubation or lysis steps, reported in degrees Celsius at the time of processing. Typical values range from 20 to 65 depending on protocol; record the active extraction temperature, not culture growth temperature.

Total duration of the active extraction/lysis procedure in minutes, measured from the start of cell disruption to DNA recovery. Record the actual processing time for this sample; typical values range from about 15 to 240 minutes.

Total amount of purified genomic DNA recovered from the fungal input after extraction, measured in nanograms at the end of the process before library preparation. Use this as a process output quality indicator; typical values depend on biomass and protocol and may range from tens to thousands of ng.

Concentration of the recovered genomic DNA, measured in ng/µL after purification and before downstream library preparation. Record the measured concentration for the final extract; typical values may range from low single digits to hundreds of ng/µL.

UV absorbance purity ratio A260/A280 measured on the purified DNA extract after extraction, used as a quality indicator for protein contamination. Typical values for clean DNA are approximately 1.7 to 2.0.

UV absorbance purity ratio A260/A230 measured on the purified DNA extract after extraction, used as a quality indicator for salt/organic contamination. Typical values for clean DNA are commonly around 2.0 to 2.2.

Qualitative assessment of the recovered DNA suitability for downstream sequencing, based on observed fragmentation, viscosity, or QC results at the end of extraction. Use this as a process-level outcome flag rather than a property of the DNA entity.

fungal_genomic_dna.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I kept only intrinsic properties of the purified genomic DNA object and removed the colliding QC fields previously generated elsewhere in the DAG. I also avoided process-level extraction details and downstream library/sequencing settings because those belong to other nodes. The revised schema retains DNA identity, linkage to the source culture, total mass, integrity/fragmentation, and storage conditions, which are sufficient to describe the DNA entity without duplicating already_generated concentration/purity metrics.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified genomic DNA sample produced by the extraction step and used as input to library preparation; use a stable lab ID such as 'gDNA-01'. Record once for this DNA entity.
Reference to the originating fungal culture or isolate for this DNA sample, recorded as a cross-link to the source biological object. Use the culture/sample ID assigned at collection time.

Total mass of the purified genomic DNA entity available after extraction and before library preparation, measured in nanograms. Typical usable amounts range from tens to many thousands of ng depending on biomass and protocol.

Numeric or instrument-derived assessment of DNA fragmentation/size integrity measured on the purified DNA sample before library preparation, if available. Record the platform-specific value used in the lab QC workflow; higher values generally indicate better integrity.

Approximate dominant fragment size of the purified genomic DNA sample in base pairs, assessed during QC before library preparation. Typical intact high-molecular-weight fungal DNA can be several kilobases or higher.
Buffer or solution in which the purified genomic DNA is stored after extraction and before library preparation, such as TE buffer or nuclease-free water.

Storage temperature for the purified genomic DNA sample before downstream library preparation, reported in degrees Celsius. Common values include 4, -20, or -80 depending on the preservation strategy.

dna_library_prep.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the conversion workflow from purified fungal genomic DNA into a sequencing-ready library: fragmentation strategy, end-repair/A-tailing, adapter ligation, size selection, amplification, input amount, and final library QC. I excluded source culture and DNA-entity purity fields because those belong upstream, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the downstream capture node. I also respected the collision notice by not reusing dna_concentration_ng_per_ul, dna_purity_a260_a280, or dna_purity_a260_a230, and instead chose library-specific QC terms that describe the process output rather than the input DNA. The result is a reproducible process schema focused on how the library was made and whether it was suitable for whole-genome sequencing.

md_schema.descr: Overall library preparation workflow used to convert fungal genomic DNA into a sequencing-ready library, recorded at the time of preparation; examples include PCR-free, transposase-based, or ligation-based methods. Use the method actually applied to this sample.

Amount of purified genomic DNA entering library preparation, measured in nanograms at the start of the process. Typical inputs vary from about 0.1 to 1000 ng depending on the kit and sequencing strategy.

Fragmentation approach applied before adapter ligation, if any, recorded during library preparation; examples include enzymatic fragmentation, acoustic shearing, or transposase-mediated fragmentation.

Target size of genomic inserts after fragmentation and size selection, reported in base pairs as specified during library preparation. Typical whole-genome sequencing libraries often target roughly 200 to 600 bp inserts.

Adapter or indexing system used during library construction, recorded as the named kit or adapter design; example format: 'Illumina TruSeq adapters'. This captures the ligation chemistry needed for sequencing compatibility.
Method used to attach adapters to fragmented DNA during library prep, such as ligase-based joining or transposase-mediated tagging, measured as part of the preparation protocol.
Number of PCR amplification cycles applied during library preparation, measured after adapter ligation and before final cleanup. Use 0 for PCR-free libraries; typical values range from 0 to about 15.
Size-selection approach used during library cleanup to enrich the desired fragment length range, such as bead-based selection or gel extraction.

Total mass of the completed sequencing library recovered at the end of preparation, measured in nanograms before capture/sequencing. This is a process output quality indicator for library construction.

Concentration of the completed sequencing library measured after cleanup and before loading onto the sequencing instrument, reported in ng/µL. Typical values vary widely with preparation scale and cleanup efficiency.

Observed library fragment size distribution summary after final cleanup, measured in base pairs and typically reported as an approximate modal or median size. Use this to confirm compatibility with the intended sequencing platform.

Whether the completed sequencing library met internal QC criteria for downstream sequencing at the end of library preparation. Use true if the library was accepted for sequencing, false if it failed QC.

sequencing_library.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I kept only intrinsic properties of the prepared sequencing library: its identity, linkage to the upstream DNA sample, adapter/index composition, insert-size profile, quantity, storage state, and QC status. I removed the colliding library_concentration_ng_per_ul field in response to the DAG-wide uniqueness constraint and avoided any upstream DNA QC or downstream capture settings. The remaining fields are library-specific and sufficient to identify, pool, and assess the prepared library object without duplicating earlier metadata.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared sequencing library entity used as input to the sequencing instrument; use a stable lab ID such as 'lib-001'. Record once for the library object.
Reference to the purified fungal genomic DNA sample from which this sequencing library was prepared, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream DNA entity ID.
Adapter and sample index combination present in the completed sequencing library, recorded as the barcode/index designation used for multiplexing; example format: 'i7-001/i5-013'.

Observed insert size of the prepared sequencing library in base pairs, measured after library construction and before sequencing. Typical whole-genome libraries often fall in the approximate range of 200 to 600 bp.
Summary descriptor of the fragment size distribution of the completed library, such as narrow, broad, bimodal, or expected peak-centered profile, assessed during library QC before sequencing.

Molar amount of the sequencing library available for loading or pooling, measured in femtomoles when quantified for sequencing setup. Typical values depend on platform and pool strategy and may range from fractions to hundreds of fmol.
Buffer or solution used to store the completed sequencing library prior to sequencing, such as Tris-EDTA or nuclease-free water.
Storage temperature for the completed sequencing library before sequencing, reported in degrees Celsius. Common values include 4, -20, or -80 depending on storage duration.
Final QC status of the prepared sequencing library immediately before sequencing, indicating whether it met acceptance criteria for loading onto the instrument.

wgs_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration for whole-genome sequencing: platform identity, manufacturer/model/serial information, run chemistry, read geometry, loading/run parameters, and run-level QC outputs. I excluded sample and library intrinsic properties because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded file format or read file location because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided the collided library_concentration_ng_per_ul field and instead focused on capture-side settings and outputs that describe how the instrument was configured and what kind of sequencing session was performed.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for whole-genome sequencing, recorded for the active capture session; example values include Illumina or equivalent vendor name.
Model name of the sequencing instrument used to read the fungal DNA library, recorded at the time of the sequencing run; example format: 'NovaSeq 6000' or similar platform model.
Instrument serial number for the sequencing device used in this capture session, recorded as the hardware identifier assigned by the facility; use a stable string such as 'SN123456'.

Sequencing reagent or chemistry version used for the run, recorded for the capture session because it affects read performance and compatibility. Example values include platform-specific chemistry revisions.

Configured read length in base pairs for each sequencing read in this whole-genome sequencing run, measured at the instrument configuration stage; typical Illumina values often include 100, 150, or 250 bp.
Read layout used for the capture session, indicating whether the sequencing run produced single-end or paired-end reads.
Lane, flowcell, or equivalent run compartment identifier used for the sequencing session, recorded as the physical run partition that generated this raw read set.

Final library loading concentration used on the sequencing instrument, reported in pmol/L at the time of run setup. Typical values depend on platform and library type and often fall within low single-digit to tens of pmol/L.

Desired cluster or spot density targeted for the sequencing run, measured in thousands per square millimeter or platform-equivalent units during run setup. Use the instrument-specific density target relevant to this sequencing session.

Total duration of the sequencing capture session from run start to completion, reported in hours. Typical whole-genome sequencing runs may last from several hours to multiple days depending on platform.

Overall quality status of the sequencing run immediately after completion, indicating whether the capture session met internal acceptance criteria before raw file handoff. Use a categorical run-level outcome.

raw_genomic_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I kept the schema limited to raw file artefact properties: file identity, format, size, read count, total bases, quality encoding, file quality metrics, and storage location. I excluded instrument configuration, library properties, and downstream computational settings. I also corrected for the reported collision by removing read_length_bp and replacing it with a non-overlapping file-level layout descriptor, while preserving the ability to validate the raw genomic data object for downstream assembly and analysis.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw genomic read file artefact produced by the sequencing run; use a stable file or sample ID such as 'reads-001'. Record once for the FASTQ-level signal object.
Technical file format of the raw sequencing reads, recorded for the signal artefact at data receipt. For this node the expected format is FASTQ or an equivalent raw-read container.

Size of the raw genomic read file on disk, measured in bytes when the file is stored or transferred. Record the actual file size for this raw signal artefact; typical values can range from millions to billions of bytes.

Total number of sequencing reads represented in the raw data file, counted after base calling and before any trimming or filtering. Typical counts may range from thousands to billions depending on sequencing depth.

Total number of bases represented in the raw read file, measured in base pairs across all reads before downstream processing. Use this to summarize dataset scale; typical values depend on run depth and read geometry.

Raw-read layout represented by the file, indicating whether the file contains single-end records, paired-end records, or a mixed/other arrangement. Record the file-level layout as stored in the raw signal artefact.
Phred quality score encoding used in the raw read file, recorded as a technical file property. Modern FASTQ data are typically Phred+33 encoded.

Average base-call quality score across all reads in the raw genomic signal file, measured from the file after sequencing and before any trimming. Typical values depend on the run but are often in the high 20s to 40s for good Illumina data.

Fraction of bases in the raw read file with a Phred quality score of at least 30, measured as a file-level quality indicator after sequencing. Values range from 0 to 1, with higher values indicating better raw read quality.

File system path, object-store URI, or repository location where the raw genomic read file is stored, recorded at data ingestion or archival time. Example formats include local paths, S3 URIs, or accession links.

genome_assembly.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the assembly workflow and assembly-specific configuration/results: assembler identity, version, input read set reference, k-mer or graph settings, contig/scaffold outcome metrics, and assembly quality indicators. I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to the Signal node, and I excluded the assembled genome object itself because those intrinsic properties belong to the Derivative node. I also avoided the collided read_length_bp field and chose assembly-specific length/statistics that describe how the reads were combined and how successful the assembly was. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I only needed to avoid semantic overlap with upstream and downstream nodes.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genome assembly software used to assemble raw fungal sequencing reads into contigs, recorded at the time of the computational process; example format: 'SPAdes'.
Version of the assembly software used for this process, recorded to support reproducibility; example format: '3.15.5'.
Identifier for the raw genomic read file set used as input to the assembly process, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream signal object. Use the raw read file ID assigned at data ingestion.

k-mer size or primary k-mer setting used during assembly, recorded as part of the assembly configuration. Typical values depend on the assembler and read length and often fall within a platform- and genome-dependent range such as 21 to 127.

Minimum contig length threshold applied when retaining assembled contigs, measured in base pairs. This setting is used during or immediately after assembly to filter short fragments; common values vary from a few hundred to a few thousand bp.
Assembly strategy or operating mode used by the assembler, such as isolate, meta, careful, or default, recorded as a categorical process setting.

Number of contigs produced by the assembly process before or after basic filtering, reported as a process output quality indicator. Lower counts often indicate more contiguous assemblies, depending on genome complexity.
Assembly N50 statistic calculated from the contigs generated by this process, reported in base pairs as a common contiguity metric. Larger values generally indicate more contiguous assemblies.

Total number of base pairs recovered in the assembly output from the raw reads, measured as the combined length of contigs/scaffolds generated by the process. Compare with expected fungal genome size to assess completeness.
Overall qualitative assessment of the assembly output immediately after the process, based on contiguity, completeness, and contamination checks. Use this as a process-level outcome indicator.

assembled_genome.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I retained only properties intrinsic to the computed assembled genome object and removed the collided contig_count and n50_bp fields. I kept identity, assembly length, scaffold structure, composition, completeness, contamination, and storage location because these describe the derived genome artifact itself rather than the upstream assembly process. I excluded assembler settings, raw read details, and process-level QC to stay within derivative territory and avoid repeating previously generated fields. The revised schema keeps the assembly reusable for downstream gene prediction while respecting cross-DAG field uniqueness.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed fungal genome assembly object produced from the raw reads; use a stable assembly ID such as 'asm-001'. Record once for the derivative genome object.
Reference to the raw genomic read file or read set from which this assembly was computed, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream signal object.

Total length of the assembled genome in base pairs, measured from the contigs/scaffolds in the final assembly object. Compare with expected fungal genome sizes, which often fall in the tens of megabases.
Number of scaffolds present in the final assembled genome object, if scaffolding was performed. Use this to describe the resolved structure of the computed genome assembly.
Fraction of bases in the assembled genome that are G or C, measured on the final assembly object. Typical fungal genomes often have species-specific GC content in the approximate range of 0.3 to 0.6.

BUSCO completeness score for the assembled genome, reported as the percentage of expected single-copy orthologs recovered in the final assembly. Typical values range from 0 to 100 and indicate assembly completeness.

Estimated contamination level in the assembled genome object, reported as a percentage of non-target or foreign sequence detected after assembly QC. Lower values are preferred and can range from 0 to 100.
Storage location or access URI for the assembled genome file, recorded when the derivative object is archived. Example formats include local paths, repository accession links, or object-store URIs.

gene_prediction.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only gene prediction workflow parameters and process outputs: prediction software identity/version, evidence/model settings, parameterization, and summary quality indicators for the predicted gene set. I excluded assembly-level properties such as contig_count and n50_bp because those belong to the assembled_genome derivative and were already reported earlier, and I excluded raw read and sequencing capture details because they are upstream. I also avoided repeating the assembled genome identifier in a way that would duplicate the downstream derivative node, instead linking the prediction process to its input assembly. The schema is tailored to let a user understand how gene models were generated from the fungal assembly and whether the prediction output is usable for biosynthetic cluster mining.

md_schema.descr: Name of the gene prediction software used to infer protein-coding genes from the assembled fungal genome, recorded at the time of the computational process; example format: 'AUGUSTUS'.
Version of the gene prediction software used for this process, recorded to support reproducibility; example format: '3.5.0'.
Identifier for the assembled genome used as input to gene prediction, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream assembly derivative.

Species model, training set, or parameter file used to calibrate gene prediction on the fungal genome, recorded during the process when applicable; example format: a related fungal species or custom model name.
Type of evidence used by the gene prediction algorithm, such as ab initio, RNA-supported, or homology-guided prediction, recorded as a categorical process setting.

Minimum predicted coding sequence or gene length threshold applied during gene prediction, measured in base pairs. Typical thresholds may range from a few dozen to several hundred bp depending on the pipeline.

Maximum intron length allowed or assumed by the gene prediction model during analysis, measured in base pairs. Record the actual setting used for this fungal genome because it influences predicted gene structures.
Total number of protein-coding genes predicted from the assembled fungal genome by this process, reported as a process output quantity. Use this as a summary of prediction yield.
Total number of predicted transcript models or isoforms generated by the gene prediction process, if applicable. Record the count actually produced by the pipeline for this assembly.
Overall qualitative assessment of the gene prediction result, based on model consistency, completeness, and downstream utility for cluster mining. Use this as a process-level outcome indicator.

predicted_genes.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included properties of the computed gene-model product itself: the gene set identifier, linkage to the source assembly, counts and coordinate statistics, annotation-ready content metrics, and storage location. I excluded gene prediction software and parameter settings because those belong to the upstream gene_prediction process, and I avoided assembly-level metrics or sequencing details because they belong to earlier nodes. I also avoided reusing contig_count and n50_bp, which were previously generated and are not intrinsic to gene models anyway. The schema is focused on the reusable predicted gene set that downstream BGC detection will consume.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the predicted gene model set produced from the assembled fungal genome; use a stable ID such as 'geneset-001'. Record once for the derivative gene object.
Reference to the assembled genome from which these gene models were inferred, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream assembly derivative.
Total number of predicted gene models in the gene set object, measured as the count of distinct genes returned by the prediction pipeline. This is an intrinsic property of the derivative gene set.
Number of predicted coding sequences or CDS records in the gene set, if separated from gene models by the pipeline. Record the actual count present in the computed gene object.
Average length of predicted gene models in base pairs, calculated across the final gene set. Typical fungal predicted genes often span roughly hundreds to several thousand bp.
Average number of exons per predicted gene model in the gene set, calculated from the computed annotation. Use this to summarize gene structure complexity.
Coordinate system or annotation file format used to represent the predicted genes, such as GFF3 or BED. Record the format of the derivative gene set for downstream reuse.
Whether translated protein sequences are included with the predicted gene set derivative. Use true if amino acid sequences were generated alongside gene models, false otherwise.

Qualitative assessment of the predicted gene set's usability for downstream biosynthetic cluster detection, based on coverage, structure, and internal consistency. Use this as a derivative-level outcome indicator.

Storage location or access URI for the predicted gene set object, recorded when the derivative is saved or archived. Example formats include local paths, repository accession links, or object-store URIs.

bgc_detection.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the biosynthetic gene cluster detection workflow and its output-level summaries: detection software identity/version, input gene set reference, detection rule/model settings, cluster class categories, and process QC. I excluded the cluster object’s intrinsic properties such as cluster coordinates or cluster count that would belong to the biosynthetic_gene_clusters derivative node, and I excluded gene prediction or assembly details because those are upstream. I also avoided repeating any already-generated fields that were not relevant to BGC detection. The schema is designed to capture how the antiSMASH-like scan was run and whether it produced actionable cluster calls for downstream gene-level annotation.

md_schema.descr: Name of the biosynthetic gene cluster detection software used to scan predicted fungal genes for secondary metabolite clusters, recorded at the time of the computational process; example format: 'antiSMASH'.
Version of the BGC detection software used for this process, recorded to support reproducibility; example format: '7.0'.
Identifier for the predicted gene set used as input to BGC detection, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream derivative gene object.
Reference database or rule set version used by the BGC detector to classify biosynthetic signatures, recorded during the process because it influences cluster calls and subclass assignment.
Operating mode or sensitivity mode used for BGC detection, such as strict, relaxed, or full analysis, recorded as a categorical process setting.

Cluster classes targeted or emphasized during the detection run, such as polyketide synthase, nonribosomal peptide synthetase, terpene, or hybrid classes, recorded as a categorical summary of the scan configuration.

Minimum genomic span required to call a biosynthetic gene cluster during detection, measured in base pairs. Typical thresholds depend on the software and cluster class and may range from a few kilobases upward.
Number of candidate biosynthetic gene clusters detected by the process before downstream annotation, reported as a process output quantity.
Summary of the biosynthetic cluster classes detected in this scan, reported as a categorical output that can include one or more class labels in a controlled form.

Overall qualitative assessment of the BGC detection result, based on model consistency, expected cluster recovery, and usefulness for downstream cluster gene annotation. Use this as a process-level outcome indicator.

biosynthetic_gene_clusters.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included intrinsic properties of the cluster-call object itself: cluster identifiers, linkage to the source gene set, genomic coordinates/span, class/subclass labels, gene counts, confidence, and storage location. I excluded BGC detection software/version and scanning settings because those belong to the upstream bgc_detection process, and I avoided assembly or read-level metrics because they are outside this node's territory. I also avoided repeating any previously generated fields that would collide semantically, focusing on the reusable cluster-call table that downstream gene-level annotation will consume.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the biosynthetic gene cluster call set produced from BGC detection; use a stable ID such as 'bgcset-001'. Record once for the derivative cluster object.
Reference to the predicted gene set from which these biosynthetic cluster calls were derived, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream gene prediction derivative.

Identifier for an individual biosynthetic gene cluster call within the call set, such as a numbered cluster label or software-generated locus name. Use this to distinguish one cluster from another within the derivative object.
Genomic start coordinate of the biosynthetic gene cluster on the assembled genome, measured in base pairs and reported on the final cluster call object.
Genomic end coordinate of the biosynthetic gene cluster on the assembled genome, measured in base pairs and reported on the final cluster call object.

Total length of the biosynthetic gene cluster span in base pairs, measured from the start and end coordinates on the final cluster call object. Typical fungal clusters can range from several kilobases to tens of kilobases.
Primary biosynthetic class assigned to the cluster call, such as NRPS, PKS, terpene, ribosomal peptide, or hybrid, recorded as an intrinsic property of the detected cluster.
More specific subclass or family designation for the cluster call, if provided by the detector, such as type I PKS or NRPS-like. Record the assigned subclass as a string.
Number of genes contained within the detected biosynthetic cluster call, counted from the derivative cluster object.

Software-derived confidence or support score for the cluster call, recorded as a numeric measure of how likely the locus is to represent a true biosynthetic gene cluster. Use the detector's native scale.

Storage location or access URI for the biosynthetic gene cluster call file or table, recorded when the derivative object is archived. Example formats include local paths, repository accession links, or object-store URIs.

gene_level_annotation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the annotation workflow settings and process outputs for assigning functions to genes within detected biosynthetic clusters: annotation software identity/version, input cluster reference, evidence sources, ontology/database settings, and summary quality indicators. I excluded cluster intrinsic properties such as coordinates and cluster class because those belong to the upstream biosynthetic_gene_clusters derivative, and I excluded the annotated gene set object’s own fields because those belong to the downstream derivative node. I also avoided repeating the output gene-count or cluster identifiers from prior nodes unless needed as cross-links. The schema is aimed at capturing how cluster genes were functionally interpreted and whether the annotations are sufficient for pathway reconstruction.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or annotation pipeline used to assign functions to genes within biosynthetic gene clusters, recorded at the time of the computational process; example format: 'InterProScan'.
Version of the cluster annotation software or pipeline used for this process, recorded to support reproducibility; example format: '5.0'.
Identifier for the biosynthetic gene cluster call set used as input to gene-level annotation, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream derivative cluster object.

Version of the functional annotation database or rule set used to infer enzyme domains, pathways, or protein families for cluster genes, recorded during the process because it determines annotation calls.
Primary evidence source used to annotate cluster genes, such as protein domain signatures, homology hits, conserved motifs, or combined evidence, recorded as a categorical process setting.
Whether gene annotations were mapped to a named ontology or controlled vocabulary such as GO, EC, or Pfam. Record the mapping type used by the process.

Minimum alignment or domain coverage threshold required to assign a functional annotation to a cluster gene, reported as a percentage used during the annotation process. Typical values may range from 0 to 100, with stricter pipelines using higher cutoffs.
Number of genes within biosynthetic clusters that received at least one functional annotation during this process, reported as a process output quantity.
Number of distinct biosynthetic pathway roles inferred across the annotated cluster genes, reported as a process output summary.

Overall qualitative assessment of the cluster gene annotation result, based on annotation coverage, consistency, and usefulness for pathway interpretation. Use this as a process-level outcome indicator.

annotated_cluster_genes.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included intrinsic properties of the annotated cluster-gene table itself: object identifier, link to the source cluster calls, per-gene identifiers, coordinates, assigned enzyme classes, predicted pathway roles, confidence/support, and storage location. I excluded annotation software, databases, and thresholds because those belong to the upstream gene_level_annotation process, and I excluded cluster detection details because those belong earlier in the workflow. I also avoided reusing any previously generated field ids that would collide semantically with cluster-level or process-level metadata, including the reported collision on cluster_identifier, so I replaced it with a gene-to-cluster reference that is unique to this node’s annotation table. The schema is tailored to the reusable annotation product consumed by downstream integration with metabolite evidence.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derivative table or object containing annotated genes from biosynthetic clusters; use a stable ID such as 'acg-001'. Record once for the annotated gene object.
Reference to the biosynthetic gene cluster call set from which these gene annotations were derived, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream cluster derivative.
Identifier for an individual gene within a biosynthetic cluster that has been functionally annotated, such as the gene locus tag or a cluster-specific gene label. Use a stable string per gene record.
Identifier of the specific biosynthetic cluster call containing this annotated gene, linking the gene annotation to the upstream cluster record without reusing a generic cluster-level field name.
Start coordinate of the annotated gene on the assembled genome, measured in base pairs and reported in the final annotated cluster gene object.
End coordinate of the annotated gene on the assembled genome, measured in base pairs and reported in the final annotated cluster gene object.
Assigned enzyme or protein class for the annotated cluster gene, such as oxidoreductase, methyltransferase, transporter, ligase, or synthase. Record the class inferred for the biosynthetic role.

Predicted functional role of the gene in the secondary metabolite pathway, such as core scaffold formation, tailoring, transport, regulation, or resistance. Record the pathway role assigned to the annotated gene.

Numeric confidence or support score for the gene-level annotation, recorded as the software- or curator-derived support value for the assigned enzyme class and pathway role. Use the native score scale when available.

Storage location or access URI for the annotated cluster gene table or file, recorded when the derivative object is archived. Example formats include local paths, repository accession links, or object-store URIs.

metabolite_isolation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only how fungal material was processed to obtain a chemical extract enriched for secondary metabolites: extraction solvent system, isolation/purification method, processing conditions, yield, and a process-level quality outcome. I excluded the source fungal culture and extract-object properties because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded raw LC-MS settings because those belong to the downstream chemical_capture node. I also avoided using cluster-related or sequencing-related field names, and I chose process-specific descriptors that help reproduce the isolation workflow and understand extract quality.

md_schema.descr: Primary extraction and isolation workflow used to recover secondary metabolites from fungal material, recorded at the time of processing; examples include solvent extraction, liquid-liquid partitioning, SPE, or preparative chromatography. Use the actual method applied to this sample.

Main solvent or solvent mixture used during metabolite extraction, recorded as the chemical system employed to solubilize secondary metabolites; example values include methanol, ethyl acetate, or methanol:water mixtures.

Mass of fungal biomass or material processed for metabolite isolation, measured in grams at the start of the extraction workflow. Typical values vary from fractions of a gram to many grams depending on culture scale.

Temperature used during metabolite extraction or isolation, reported in degrees Celsius at the time the sample was processed. Typical values range from 4 to room temperature or higher depending on protocol.

Total active extraction or isolation time in minutes, measured from initiation of solvent contact or purification to recovery of the crude or enriched extract. Typical values range from minutes to several hours.

Number of discrete purification steps applied during metabolite isolation, such as solvent partitioning, SPE cleanup, and chromatographic fractionation. Record the total number of steps used to enrich the target metabolites.

Mass of the recovered metabolite extract or purified fraction obtained at the end of the isolation process, measured in milligrams. This is a process output quality indicator for the isolation workflow.

Qualitative assessment of how enriched the final metabolite extract is in secondary metabolites versus bulk matrix components, evaluated at the end of the isolation process. Use a categorical quality judgment.

Identifier for the replicate isolation run associated with this metabolite extraction, if the workflow was repeated on independent biomass or technical replicates. Use a stable string such as 'replicate_1'.
Overall quality status of the isolation process, indicating whether the extract was suitable for downstream chemical analysis. Use this as the process-level outcome indicator.

metabolite_extract.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included intrinsic properties of the prepared chemical extract itself: extract identity, source biomass reference, solvent composition, concentration/enrichment, quantity, storage state, and accession/location. I excluded extraction protocol parameters because those belong to metabolite_isolation, and I excluded LC-MS instrument settings because those belong to chemical_capture. I also avoided any cluster or sequencing terminology, and I kept the schema focused on what downstream chemical analysis needs to know about the extract object as received by the instrument.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the chemical extract entity produced by the isolation step and used for instrumental analysis; use a stable lab ID such as 'extract-001'. Record once for the extract object.
Reference to the originating fungal culture or biomass from which this extract was prepared, recorded as a cross-link to the source biological object ID.
Solvent or solvent mixture present in the final metabolite extract, recorded as the composition used to store or reconstitute the sample before analysis; example format: 'methanol:water 80:20'.

Concentration of the metabolite extract prepared for instrumental analysis, reported in mg/mL at the time of measurement or reconstitution. Typical values depend on the assay and may range from low microgram to tens of mg/mL.
Total mass of recovered extract available for analysis, measured in milligrams at the end of isolation. Use this to describe the quantity of the chemical entity.
Volume of the extract solution prepared for analysis, measured in microliters. Record the actual sample volume loaded or archived for the chemical capture step.
Storage temperature for the chemical extract before instrumental analysis, reported in degrees Celsius. Common values include 4, -20, or -80 depending on short- or long-term storage.
Buffer, solvent, or vial medium used to store the chemical extract before analysis, such as methanol, acetonitrile, or another compatible solvent system.
Qualitative or semi-quantitative assessment of how enriched the final extract is in secondary metabolites relative to the starting biomass, recorded as a categorical property of the extract entity.
Storage location or access URI for the metabolite extract entity or sample record, recorded when the extract is archived. Example formats include local paths, LIMS links, or repository accessions.

chemical_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration for chemical analysis: instrument manufacturer/model/serial, ionization and acquisition settings, chromatography parameters, scan range, and run-level QC. I excluded extract composition and concentration because those belong to the metabolite_extract entity, and I excluded raw file format/path because those belong to the downstream raw chemical signal node. I also avoided any sequencing or genome-related fields, and I focused on the actively controlled LC-MS settings that define how the chemical signatures were captured from the extract.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the analytical instrument used for chemical capture, recorded for the active LC-MS or equivalent session; example values include Thermo Fisher, Agilent, Waters, or Bruker.
Model name of the analytical instrument used to measure the fungal metabolite extract, recorded at the time of the capture session; example format: 'Q Exactive Orbitrap' or equivalent platform model.
Instrument serial number for the analytical device used in this chemical capture session, recorded as the hardware identifier assigned by the facility; use a stable string such as 'SN123456'.
Ionization polarity or mode used during chemical capture, recorded as the actively configured setting for the run; common values include positive and negative electrospray ionization.
Mass spectrometry acquisition mode used for the capture session, such as full scan, data-dependent acquisition, or data-independent acquisition.
Chromatographic separation method used before mass analysis, recorded as the configured LC method for the run; example formats include reversed-phase LC or HILIC.
Mass-to-charge scan range configured for the capture session, reported as the analyzed m/z window across the acquisition. Typical ranges depend on the instrument and may span roughly 50 to 2000 m/z.

Configured or expected mass accuracy for the chemical capture run, reported in parts per million when the instrument method specifies it. Typical values for high-resolution LC-MS may be in the low ppm range.
Liquid chromatography flow rate used during the capture session, reported in milliliters per minute. Typical LC-MS methods often use values from about 0.1 to 1.0 mL/min depending on column and setup.
Total duration of the chemical capture session, reported in minutes from injection to end of acquisition. This is a run-level setting for the instrument session, not a sample property.
Overall qualitative status of the chemical capture run immediately after acquisition, indicating whether the instrument session produced usable data for downstream signal processing.

raw_chemical_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only properties of the raw chemical data artefact itself, but I renamed the colliding generic fields to be signal-specific. I kept file identity, acquisition dimensionality, and technical quality metrics, while excluding instrument configuration from chemical_capture and downstream processed feature tables. The collision notice required me to avoid file_format, file_size_bytes, mass_accuracy_ppm, and storage_uri exactly, so I replaced them with raw_chemical-specific field names that preserve the same semantic layer without duplicating prior DAG metadata. The schema is still focused on verifying raw signal validity and usability for feature extraction.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw chemical signal file artefact produced by the analytical instrument; use a stable file or sample ID such as 'chemraw-001'. Record once for the raw signal object.
Technical file format of the raw chemical data, recorded at data receipt or archiving. For this node the expected format may be vendor raw, mzML, mzXML, or an equivalent raw-signal container.

Size of the raw chemical signal file on disk, measured in bytes when the file is stored or transferred. Record the actual file size for this raw artefact; typical values can range from millions to many billions of bytes depending on run length and scan density.

Total number of chromatographic or MS scans represented in the raw chemical file, counted after acquisition and before any feature extraction. Use this to summarize the data density of the raw signal artefact.
Total chromatographic time span covered by the raw chemical signal file, measured in minutes from the first to last scan. Typical LC-MS runs can span several minutes to multiple hours.
Number of tandem MS levels or distinct MS levels represented in the raw file, such as MS1 only or MS1+MS2. Record the actual acquisition depth present in the signal artefact.

Average signal-to-noise ratio observed across the raw chemical file, measured as a file-level technical quality indicator before any peak picking or filtering. Higher values generally indicate cleaner raw data.

Observed or estimated mass accuracy of the raw chemical signal file, reported in parts per million as a technical quality metric after acquisition. Typical high-resolution data may fall in the low ppm range.

File system path, object-store URI, or repository location where the raw chemical signal file is stored, recorded at data ingestion or archival time. Example formats include local paths, S3 URIs, or accession links.

chemical_feature_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the feature-extraction workflow and its outputs: software identity/version, input raw signal reference, peak-picking and deconvolution settings, feature-detection thresholds, and process-level quality indicators. I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the raw_chemical_signal node, and I excluded the resulting feature table object itself because its intrinsic properties belong to the metabolite_features derivative node. I also avoided repeating any collided generic file fields such as file_format, file_size_bytes, mass_accuracy_ppm, and storage_uri, and instead used process-specific chemical feature extraction metadata that describes how peaks and candidate compounds were derived from the raw signal.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to process raw chemical signals into peaks and metabolite features, recorded at the time of the computational process; example format: 'MZmine'.
Version of the feature extraction software used for this process, recorded to support reproducibility; example format: '3.0'.
Identifier for the raw chemical signal file used as input to feature processing, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream signal object.
Algorithm or method used to detect chromatographic peaks from the raw chemical signal, recorded as a process setting; examples include centroid-based or wavelet-based peak picking.
Method used to deconvolute overlapping signals or adduct groups during feature extraction, recorded as a categorical process setting.

Minimum signal intensity threshold used to call a peak as a feature, recorded in the instrument's intensity units or pipeline-native units. Typical thresholds depend on the dataset and should be the actual value used in processing.
Minimum chromatographic peak duration required for feature detection, reported in seconds. This setting filters short noise peaks and is measured during the processing step.
Mass difference tolerance used for feature grouping or separation in Daltons, recorded as a process parameter when supported by the pipeline. Typical values are small fractions of a Dalton.
Total number of chromatographic peaks detected from the raw chemical signal by this process, reported as a process output quantity.
Total number of candidate compounds or feature groups retained after feature processing, reported as a process output summary.
Overall qualitative assessment of the feature extraction result, based on peak quality, deconvolution success, and downstream usability. Use this as the process-level outcome indicator.

metabolite_features.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included properties of the computed feature table itself: feature table ID, link to the raw signal, dimensionality, abundance/intensity statistics, adduct/isotope representation, confidence, and storage location. I excluded peak-picking algorithms and thresholds because those belong to the upstream chemical_feature_processing process, and I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the Signal node. I also avoided reusing generic file metadata fields that collided earlier, focusing on the reusable feature table object needed for compound annotation.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed metabolite feature table produced from raw chemical signal processing; use a stable ID such as 'feat-001'. Record once for the derivative feature object.
Reference to the raw chemical signal file from which this feature table was computed, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream signal object.

Total number of detected features represented in the final metabolite feature table, measured as the count of ions/peaks retained after processing. This is an intrinsic property of the derivative object.
Number of input samples or runs represented in the feature table, if the table is aggregated across more than one run. Record the actual number of samples captured in the derivative object.
Average abundance or intensity across all retained metabolite features in the table, measured in the pipeline's native intensity units. This summarizes the scale of the computed feature set.

Observed intensity range across features in the table, recorded as a concise string or numeric summary such as minimum and maximum intensity values. Use this to describe the spread of the derivative feature set.
Whether adduct annotations were assigned to the features in the table. Use true if adduct labels are present, false otherwise.
Whether isotope annotations were assigned to the features in the table. Use true if isotope labels are present, false otherwise.

Numeric confidence or overall support score for the computed feature table, reflecting how robustly peaks and compounds were represented after processing. Use the native pipeline scale when available.

Storage location or access URI for the computed metabolite feature table, recorded when the derivative object is archived. Example formats include local paths, repository accession links, or object-store URIs.

compound_annotation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the compound-annotation workflow and its outputs: annotation software identity/version, input feature-table reference, library/formula search settings, confidence criteria, and process-level quality indicators. I excluded the annotated metabolite object’s intrinsic properties because those belong to the downstream derivative node, and I excluded raw signal or instrument settings because those belong earlier in the workflow. I also avoided reusing any earlier collided file metadata fields. The schema is designed to capture how putative identities were assigned to features and whether the annotation step was sufficiently supported for downstream biological interpretation.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or annotation pipeline used to assign putative compound identities to metabolite features, recorded at the time of the computational process; example format: 'SIRIUS'.
Version of the compound annotation software used for this process, recorded to support reproducibility; example format: '5.0'.
Identifier for the metabolite feature table used as input to compound annotation, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream derivative feature object.
Name of the spectral or compound reference library used during annotation, recorded as part of the process configuration; example format: 'GNPS', 'MassBank', or a custom in-house library.
Version or release of the reference library used during compound annotation, recorded to support reproducibility; example format: a dated release or version string.
Whether annotation relied on molecular formula search, library match, or both, recorded as the active search strategy for the process.
Mass tolerance used when matching metabolite features against reference compounds or formulas, reported in parts per million. Typical high-resolution searches often use a small ppm window.

Minimum score or confidence threshold required to accept a putative compound annotation, recorded as the cutoff used by the annotation process. Use the native score scale of the pipeline when available.
Number of metabolite features that received at least one putative compound annotation during this process, reported as a process output quantity.
Overall qualitative assessment of the compound annotation result, based on match quality, library coverage, and support for downstream interpretation. Use this as the process-level outcome indicator.

annotated_metabolites.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I kept only intrinsic properties of the annotated metabolite set itself. The collision notice meant I had to avoid annotation_confidence_score, so I replaced it with metabolite-specific support metrics that still describe the output record without duplicating prior gene-annotation fields. I excluded upstream compound_annotation software and thresholds, as well as raw feature or capture properties, because those belong to other nodes. The schema focuses on the reusable annotated metabolite table and its evidence quality for downstream linking to BGCs.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derivative object containing putatively annotated metabolites; use a stable ID such as 'amet-001'. Record once for the annotated metabolite object.
Reference to the metabolite feature table from which these annotated metabolites were derived, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream derivative feature object.
Identifier for an individual putatively annotated metabolite record within the derivative table, such as a feature ID or annotation row ID. Use a stable string per record.

Putative compound identity assigned to the annotated metabolite, recorded as the candidate name returned by the annotation pipeline or curator. This is a tentative identification, not a confirmed structure.
Molecular formula assigned or inferred for the annotated metabolite, reported as a string such as C10H12O2 when supported by the annotation evidence.
Observed adduct form associated with the annotated metabolite feature, such as [M+H]+ or [M-H]-, recorded as part of the annotation record.

Numeric support score for the putative metabolite annotation, recorded as the native score or posterior support value from the annotation pipeline. Use this metabolite-level support metric instead of a generic annotation confidence field.
Primary evidence type supporting the putative metabolite identity, such as library match, formula match, or combined evidence, recorded as an intrinsic property of the annotation record.
Whether tandem MS evidence was available and used for the annotated metabolite call. Use true if MS/MS spectra contributed to the annotation, false otherwise.

Storage location or access URI for the annotated metabolite table or object, recorded when the derivative is archived. Example formats include local paths, repository accession links, or object-store URIs.

integrative_bgc_metabolite_linking.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the integrative linking workflow: input references to annotated gene and metabolite derivatives, linking method, evidence types, scoring thresholds, candidate link counts, and process-level quality. I excluded intrinsic properties of the linked map object because those belong to the downstream derivative node, and I excluded all upstream cluster, gene, and metabolite annotation details because those belong to prior nodes. I also avoided any already collided field ids such as annotation_confidence_score. The schema is focused on how gene-cluster and metabolite evidence were combined to infer candidate biosynthetic relationships.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software, pipeline, or analysis framework used to link annotated biosynthetic cluster genes with annotated metabolites, recorded at the time of the computational process; example format: 'custom_integration_pipeline'.
Version of the linking software or pipeline used for this process, recorded to support reproducibility; example format: '1.0'.
Identifier for the annotated cluster gene set used as input to the integrative linking analysis, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream derivative gene object.
Identifier for the annotated metabolite set used as input to the integrative linking analysis, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream derivative metabolite object.

Primary method used to infer links between biosynthetic gene clusters and candidate metabolites, recorded as the active analysis strategy; examples include correlation, rule-based matching, or network-based integration.
Types of evidence integrated to support cluster-metabolite links, recorded as a categorical summary of the sources used in the analysis.
Minimum score or confidence threshold required to accept a candidate cluster-metabolite link, recorded as the cutoff used by the integrative process. Use the native scale used by the pipeline.
Number of candidate biosynthetic gene cluster to metabolite links produced by the integration analysis, reported as a process output quantity.
Whether the linking analysis explicitly evaluated novelty of cluster-metabolite relationships, recorded as the process mode used to prioritize candidate new pathways or metabolites.

Overall qualitative assessment of the linking result, based on coherence of gene and metabolite evidence, specificity of assignments, and downstream utility. Use this as the process-level outcome indicator.

bgc_metabolite_map.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included intrinsic properties of the integrated map object itself: map identifier, links to the source annotated gene and metabolite sets, per-link records, link type, confidence, novelty assessment, and storage location. I excluded integration software, methods, and thresholds because those belong to the upstream integrative_bgc_metabolite_linking process, and I excluded upstream annotation details because they belong to prior derivative nodes. I also avoided reusing any already generated field ids that would collide semantically. The schema is intended for the final reusable mapping object that ties cluster genetics to candidate metabolite products.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the integrated biosynthetic gene cluster to metabolite map object; use a stable ID such as 'map-001'. Record once for the derivative map object.
Reference to the annotated cluster gene set used to build this integrated map, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream derivative gene object.
Reference to the annotated metabolite set used to build this integrated map, recorded as a cross-link to the upstream derivative metabolite object.
Identifier for an individual cluster-to-metabolite link or row within the integrated map, such as a numbered entry or analyst-generated mapping label. Use a stable string per mapped relationship.
Identifier of the biosynthetic gene cluster associated with the mapped metabolite product, recorded as the cluster label used in the upstream cluster or annotation tables.
Identifier of the metabolite or metabolite feature associated with the mapped biosynthetic cluster, recorded as the stable ID used in the annotated metabolite set.
Type of relationship assigned in the integrated map, such as direct match, partial match, putative match, or candidate novel pathway association.

Numeric confidence score for the cluster-to-metabolite link recorded in the final integrated map, reflecting the strength of combined genomic and chemical evidence. Use the native score scale produced by the analysis.
Whether the mapped cluster-metabolite relationship is considered novel relative to known references, recorded as a binary derivative property of the final map.

Storage location or access URI for the final biosynthetic gene cluster to metabolite map object, recorded when the derivative is archived. Example formats include local paths, repository accession links, or object-store URIs.
